lines.say: The immune system must tell self from non-self.
An antigen is a molecule the adaptive system recognises, like a surface protein.
The small part a receptor actually binds is the epitope.
Innate is the security guard. Adaptive is the detective with a filing cabinet.
Innate immunity is fast, general, and doesn't improve with repeat exposure.
Toll like receptors spot molecules common to microbes, like lipopolysaccharide.
Neutrophils arrive first. Macrophages engulf pathogens by phagocytosis.

draw.alt: Phagocyte engulfing bacterium into a vesicle that fuses with a lysosome

lines.say: NK cells kill cells with too little MHC class one. Interferons warn neighbour cells.
Inflammation: histamine widens and leaks vessels. Redness, heat, swelling, pain.
B cells mature in bone marrow. T cells mature in the thymus.
Each lymphocyte has one receptor type, made by random gene shuffling.
An antigen selects the one matching cell. It's a shop picking from stock.

draw.alt: Many different lymphocytes; antigen selects one

lines.say: That cell divides into a clone of effector cells and memory cells.

draw.alt: Selected cell divides into many copies

lines.say: Cells that react to self are removed, giving self tolerance.
T cells can't see free antigen. It must be shown on MHC.
MHC class one is on almost all nucleated cells. It shows what's made inside.
MHC class two is on antigen presenting cells, like dendritic cells.
Class times CD number is always 8. One times 8, two times 4.

draw.alt: CD8 cytotoxic T cell reads MHC I; CD4 helper T cell reads MHC II

lines.say: Helper T cells release cytokines that activate both B cells and cytotoxic T cells.
Cytotoxic T cells kill infected cells using perforin and trigger apoptosis.
B cells, with T cell help, become plasma cells that pour out antibodies.
HIV destroys helper T cells, so both arms fail.
An antibody is a Y: two heavy chains, two light chains, and two binding sites.

draw.alt: Y-shaped antibody with variable tips and constant stem

lines.say: Antibodies don't kill directly. Remember NOAC.
Neutralisation, opsonisation, agglutination and complement activation.
IgM makes the first move. IgG crosses the placenta. IgA is in saliva. IgE, eek, allergy.
Primary response: a lag of days, then a small peak around 20 units.
Second dose of X: anti X jumps to 450. Memory cells were ready.

draw.alt: Small primary peak then much larger secondary peak

lines.say: Antigen Y gave only a small primary response. Memory is specific.
Active immunity: you make it, and it lasts. Passive: you're lent it, and it fades.
Vaccines trigger a primary response and memory cells, without causing disease.
